title: Why Continuous Improvement Needs Better Data
description:
Kaizen workshops often feel like progress, yet the same losses return a few weeks later. This episode is for lean leaders, plant engineers and manufacturing IT teams who want continuous improvement that lasts. Learn how to connect ERP, MES, machine data and shop-floor knowledge into a reliable PDCA check step that shows which countermeasures actually hold.
In this episode
00:00 – Why kaizen events lose momentum05:36 – Lean as a learning system10:32 – Why improvement programs stall14:57 – PDCA needs a reliable check step30:43 – ERP, MES, machine data and the shop floor54:37 – The data model behind continuous improvement65:40 – Scenario: reducing changeover loss84:48 – A practical Microsoft data path
Key takeaways
Continuous improvement stalls when the PDCA check step lacks connected evidence, because completed actions are not the same as learning.ERP shows intent, MES shows execution, machine data shows physical behavior and operators add meaning, so improvement needs all four linked through a shared data model.Microsoft Azure, Fabric and Power BI can carry that evidence chain, but the factory itself must define what a stop, a changeover or good output means.
Worth quoting
“Treating OE as a root cause answer is like treating a warning light as a repair manual. It tells you where to look. It doesn't tell you what to change.” – Mirko Peters (24:58)
“If not, they adapt or stop it. Stopping a weak countermeasure isn't failure. It's preventing a weak habit from becoming standard.” – Mirko Peters (08:54)
